title: SIM-Swap Attacks and Why SMS Codes Are Weak
summary: In a SIM-swap, an attacker convinces your mobile carrier to move your number to their device, then uses SMS codes to reset accounts and bypass text-based two-factor login.
blocks: In a SIM-swap, an attacker convinces your mobile carrier to move your number to their device, then uses SMS codes to reset accounts and bypass text-based two-factor login.
Because of this, SMS is the weakest form of two-factor authentication. An app-based authenticator or a hardware security key is far harder to hijack.
Add a carrier PIN or port-freeze where available, and move important accounts off SMS codes to an authenticator app or security key.
